ui.landing.lead: Otonari helps neighbors in the same building or block in Japan lend and borrow things, without a language barrier. Nobody types a message: everyone reads polite words in their own language.
ui.landing.problemTitle: Neighbors live a few meters apart, but rarely ask
ui.landing.problem1Text: People new to Japan often need something, but not having the words makes it hard to ask.
ui.landing.problem2Text: Nobody wants to be a burden (遠慮, enryo), or to chase someone about an overdue item.
ui.landing.problem3Text: Meanwhile a futon dryer or a stepladder waits next door, in the home of someone who would be glad to help.
ui.landing.vision: A neighborhood where anyone can ask, and anyone can help. Where a borrowed takoyaki maker becomes the first hello, and neighbors who share no language still share a wall, a shelf and a thank-you.
ui.landing.step1Text: Create an account, scan the poster in your building, and choose a nickname.
ui.landing.step2Text: Choose the item, day and time. You see exactly what your neighbor will read.
ui.landing.step3Text: Hand it over at the entrance or the mailboxes. A photo shows its condition.
ui.landing.step4Text: One more photo and a thank-you. The item is back on the shelf.
ui.landing.promise1Text: Every message is a fixed phrase, written by people. No machine translation.
ui.landing.promise2Text: Otonari reminds politely, so a lender never has to.
ui.landing.promise3Text: Neighbors see only your nickname, never your email or room number. Only people who see the poster get the code.
ui.landing.promise4Text: Both sides see the same condition at handover and at return.
ui.landing.promise5Text: Large text and buttons, read-aloud, and Easy Japanese.
ui.landing.itemsText: Things you need once or twice a year, a few steps from your door.
ui.landing.buildingText: Upstairs, downstairs, across the hall: every home has something to share. You meet in person at the entrance. The words are already taken care of.
ui.landing.buildingAlt: Drawing: an apartment building in Japan with neighbors at their windows, and two of them handing over a box at the entrance
ui.landing.placesTitle: From one building to the whole block
ui.landing.placesText: Each neighborhood has its own shelf, for the people who live there.
ui.landing.placeBuildingText: Neighbors from every floor share one shelf.
ui.landing.placeBlockText: Detached houses on the same streets can share one too.
ui.landing.placeSpotText: By the entrance, the bicycles or the notice board. Never at your door.

tips.beforeRequest: Tip: in Japan, it's polite to return things clean and on time. A small thank-you snack is a nice touch, but never required.
tips.atHandover: Tip: a short bow and "arigatou gozaimasu" goes a long way.
tips.atReturn: Tip: if you'll be late, tap "Running a little late" before the due time — it's much better than silence.
tips.forLender: Your neighbor may speak a different language. Don't worry — Otonari shows everything in their language.
